options: Part of a line between two endpoints
A path extending forever both ways
questions.explanation: A segment is the straight piece of a line that stops at two endpoints.
questions.misconception: The endless paths are lines, and one-end paths are rays — a segment has exactly two endpoints and stops.

questions.prompt: Why can you measure a segment but not a line?
options: A segment has two endpoints to measure between
questions.explanation: Because a segment stops at both ends, it has a definite length; a line never stops.
questions.misconception: Measurability comes from the endpoints stopping the path — thickness and length of drawing do not matter.

questions.prompt: A segment has endpoints at points A and B. How is it named?
questions.explanation: Name a segment by its two endpoints: segment AB.
questions.misconception: Line and ray have different arrowhead rules — a segment uses just its two endpoint names, in either order.

questions.prompt: What kind of figure has sides made of segments?
questions.explanation: Polygons like triangles and rectangles have sides that are segments.
questions.misconception: Points, lines, and rays are not closed shapes — a polygon needs a closed chain of segment sides.

questions.prompt: How do you DRAW a segment (unlike a line)?
options: Solid dots at both ends, no arrowheads
A dot at one end and an arrowhead at the other
questions.explanation: Segments use two solid endpoint dots and no arrowheads.
questions.misconception: Arrowheads mean 'keeps going' — a segment's solid dots mean 'stops here'.
